title: Leaderboard
description:
Write `std::vector<int> topScores(std::vector<int> scores, std::size_t count)` that returns the `count` highest scores, highest first. If there are fewer than `count` scores, return them all (still sorted).

Then write `int rankOf(const std::vector<int>& scores, int score)`: the 1-based position `score` would have on the full leaderboard, where rank 1 is the highest. Equal scores share a rank. (The rank is one more than the number of scores that are strictly higher.)

Use standard algorithms rather than hand-written loops for `topScores`: `std::sort` with `std::greater{}`, then `resize`. For `rankOf`, a range-based loop that counts the strictly higher scores is fine. (After the next lesson you could also write it as one `std::count_if` with a lambda that captures `score`.)
hints: Sort highest first with `std::sort(scores.begin(), scores.end(), std::greater{});`, then shrink the vector with `resize(count)` only when it is longer than `count`.
For the rank, loop over the scores counting the ones strictly higher than `score`, and add 1. The vector does not need to be sorted for that.
